title: The flitter, second take: nothing but nectar, and it cannot find enough
question: It no longer eats the bed -- but it starves out. Is an animal that appears only where the bed is flowering the right shape, or should a flower be easier to find?
context_md:
**This replaces card `20260911T044416498Z-cec12a`** -- same three strips, same bed, new animal. (The queue stores a card as written and has no way to edit one in place, so this is a new card rather than the old one updated.)

**What changed since that card.** There the flitter was a pollinator that ate its own flowers: it bred into the hundreds off leaf and took the bed from **960 plant cells to 566 and 34 standing flowers to 4**, against the same bed with no flitter in it. A strong *taste* for nectar cannot stop that, because at any setting a leaf is still worth something. So the mouth is a switch now: **nectar and nothing else** -- leaf, fruit, seed, a corpse and a drained flower all pay it exactly zero.

**The bed is safe.** Over a full session with flitters on it, plant cells and standing flowers come through in the same shape as the bed with none -- on all three seeds, better rather than worse. Flowers eaten by a flitter over 120,000 frames: **0**, where the ants on the same bed eat 3 to 9.

**And it starves out, on every bed and every seed.** Founded on its own it never breeds once; released beside the flowers it lives a while and dies. Over a whole session a flitter reaches a bloom **3 to 20 times** when it would need to do so constantly. I followed one for two thousand frames with a full flower nine cells away: **it never got closer than nine**, drifted away as often as toward, and spent the last eight hundred frames stuck in the air over a single cell until it died.

**Two separate things are in that, and I would like to know which you want fixed.** One is *finding*: seeing a flower from across the room is not the same as arriving at one, and a flower is a single cell in a bed that holds a few dozen -- the same problem as your bigger-flowers ask, from the other side. The other is a real bug, filed rather than fixed: **water is exactly as heavy as an animal here, so anything that hops and comes down on water hangs in the air and starves there.** It is most of how a flitter dies and most of how the older hopper dies too.

**Still hand-authored, still carries no pollen.** And the lab still opens on ANIMALS WEAR BY COLONY, so the pale blue-white body only shows once you cycle to OWN COLOUR -- in these strips the flitters are the pale blue ones and the ants the darker.
